messages:
From: Alyssa May <alyssa@claritymedia.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Encoder switchover contingency + post-event clip gating (Zoom/ON24)

Thanks team — quick heads up as we finalize run of show for Wednesday's joint webinar. Our on-site engineer flagged a potential license hiccup with the primary encoder at T-30 that would force a live switchover to a backup SRT encoder. Before we panic our producer, can you confirm the following controls are in place on your side: 

- Seamless handoff between Zoom RTMP ingest and ON24 bridge (we need < 8s blackout).
- Registrant token continuity so returning viewers don't have to re-auth.
- Clear policy for mid-event clip extraction (sponsor wants first-10-min highlight for paid social) — we need gating + watermark timing.

We're happy to trigger a manual switchover from the truck but need your ops checklist and an approval flow for the clip (clarify watermark / sponsor credit). Attaching the truck's preliminary checklist for context.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Producer, Clarity Media
ony-site-ops@claritymedia.com

[Attachment: truck-ops-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa May <alyssa@claritymedia.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Encoder switchover contingency + post-event clip gating (Zoom/ON24)

Thanks Alyssa — good catch. High level answers below and I've attached our quick-action checklist for the webinar ops team. Full run: see Drive link.

- RTMP -> ON24: we have a pre-configured fallback bridge. If the primary RTMP drops, the router will re-point to the backup SRT endpoint and ON24 will ingest via the secondary bridge. Expected glitch window: 6-9s depending on buffer. We'll run a hard-switch test on Wed at T-120.

- Registrant tokens: Zoom session tokens are short-lived but ON24 preserves registrant state if we pass the same registrant id in the bridge handshake. Our plan: session token refresh via the web-hook at T-5 and an id-mapper we maintain in the staging DB to avoid re-auth flows. Laura will validate the token-refresh script.

- Clip gating / watermark: proposed policy in draft (attached): sponsor clips require express written approval within 48h of the event; watermark must be applied at clip render start (3s fade-in) and include sponsor credit + event name. We can automate watermark insertion during the rendering job; Ben will confirm rendition templates and H.264 passthrough constraints.

Action items (short):
1) Ben: confirm H.264 passthrough + watermark overlay timing (by Mon EOD).
2) Laura: run session-token end-to-end test in staging (T-120 run) and confirm registrant continuity.
3) Marissa: get sponsor sign-off form (we'll use DocuSign link) and confirm which 0-10m clip window they want.
4) Alyssa: confirm truck will pause any clip extraction until we have written approval (48h window).

Attaching: encoder-switchover-checklist.xlsx, clip-gating-policy-draft.docx

Hannah Schmitt
Events Lead, Redwood Inference
--

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Encoder switchover contingency + post-event clip gating (Zoom/ON24)

Quick tech confirm — quoting Hannah below: 

> - Clip gating / watermark: proposed policy in draft (attached): sponsor clips require express written approval within 48h of the event; watermark must be applied at clip render start (3s fade-in) and include sponsor credit + event name. We can automate watermark insertion during the rendering job; Ben will confirm rendition templates and H.264 passthrough constraints.

Confirmed: our live passthrough pipeline supports overlay with zero re-encode only when the overlay is alpha-channel hardware-assisted in the encoder. The truck's backup SRT encoder does not support hardware alpha overlays in passthrough mode — that means if we need to apply watermark on the backup path we'll have to re-render the clip (adds ~10-15s render latency for short clips). For the 0-10m highlight the render job will complete in ~45s on our render pool if submitted immediately; that should be fine for pre-scheduled social posts but not instantaneous break highlights.

Risk: if we execute a live switchover and need an immediate clip for live social, we should agree to either accept a transient 12-20s re-render or pre-authorize a low-latency push (no watermark) until the approved clip is produced. 

I'll run a quick render mock on Monday to confirm timings.

Ben
Senior Streaming Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alyssa — thanks for flagging and thanks team for the quick turnaround. Two small asks to finalize the sponsor side: 

1) Can Clarity confirm in writing (email is fine) whether they will accept a 45s post-event clip turnaround with watermark (preferred) OR require an immediate unwatermarked push for live social (we will need a signed waiver for any unwatermarked distribution).

2) Please fill the small approval checkbox on the DocuSign I just created (link below) so legal has a record. I'll only move forward on extraction when we have that signed form.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/clarity-redwood-clip-approval
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_encoder_checklist

If we get the sign-off today, Ben and I will run a dry render in staging tomorrow and confirm the final template.
